A little about me

I'm Aditi. I live in Tokha, Kathmandu, and I'm starting out as a graphic designer and video editor.

I went to Gandruk once and felt so good. Nature heals me. It feels like a detox.

That feeling is what I want my work to carry: warm, calm, and a little handmade.

I design in Canva and edit in CapCut. Everything below is built from photos I took myself on trips around Nepal. I'm happy to learn the rest of your toolkit.

The warm look

Drag the line. I want every trek photo to feel like the same warm afternoon.

straight from my phonewarmer, softer

Same photo on both sides. The right side has lifted greens, a little gold in the light, and softer corners. Nothing fake added, just the afternoon as it felt.

this is a sketch of the grade. The real one I'd tune by eye in CapCut and Canva.

Brand, print and a map

practice for a made-up trek called Slow Trails

Photos are only half the job. I also made the things a trekking company needs around the photos: a logo, a few rules, a flyer, a map and stickers. The trek is invented, so every detail on the flyer is a placeholder.

The small rulebook

Moss#2F4F3E
Paper#F2E8D5
Marigold#E0A93B
River#3F7A7A
Brick#A8322A
AaFraunces, for headlines
AaDM Sans, for the words people read
AaCaveat, for little notes by hand
  1. One photo, one idea. Let the picture do the talking.
  2. Warm, never fake. No filters that change what the place looked like.
  3. Short words. If you can't read it while walking, cut it.

    A day with me

    The job runs 10 to 5, from home. Here is how I'd like a normal day to go.

    1. 10:00Coffee, then the planSee what's coming up on the trails and what the team needs most.
    2. 10:30Pick five photosChoose the best, let the rest go without guilt.
    3. 12:00Make the post in CanvaOne photo, a few honest words, a bit of hand lettering where it helps.
    4. 2:00Cut a reel in CapCutOne idea, a calm pace, a clean end card.
    5. 4:00Tidy up and plan tomorrowName the files properly, reply to notes, send a draft.
    6. 5:00Laptop closed, go outsideSome of my best ideas arrive on the walk.
    right now in Tokha, Kathmandu

    Nepal time. Your 10 to 5 is my 10 to 5.

    What I haven't done yet

    I haven't worked from a brand guide, cut footage from a real trek, or designed for a client.

    What I have: an eye for a calm frame, a folder of my own trail photos, and these finished pieces. I'll ask early when I'm unsure and send drafts often.
